proposal.title: Engagement Proposal — Rapid Organisational Diagnostic
proposal.body:
PROPOSAL — RAPID ORGANISATIONAL DIAGNOSTIC
For: {{ORG}} · Attn: {{CONTACT}} · Date: {{DATE}}
From: Rahul K. Vimal — OD Consultant & C4D Practitioner, Delhi

1 · WHAT YOU TOLD ME
[Write their problem in THEIR OWN WORDS from the call. Quote them. Do not
paraphrase into consultant language.]

2 · WHAT I WILL DO
A diagnosis before any solution: interviews with board, staff and field
(6–8 people), review of your documents (policies, reports, formats), and
direct observation of how work actually moves. I look before I fix.

3 · WHAT YOU RECEIVE
· A scored organisational capacity baseline (my assessment instrument,
 four domains — your starting point, measured, not guessed)
· A written diagnostic report in plain language your team can read
· A feedback session with leadership: findings first, priorities agreed together
· An action plan — a small number of changes your team can realistically
 adopt, with measurable indicators

4 · WHAT I NEED FROM YOU
One focal point for scheduling · honest access to people and documents ·
leadership present at the feedback session · an owner named for each change.

5 · TIMELINE
2–3 weeks from start date.

6 · INVESTMENT
Pilot rate: ₹45,000 (standard rate for this diagnostic: ₹75,000–1,20,000).
I am building documented case evidence in this sector, so my first five
engagements run at this pilot rate. In exchange I ask for a written case
study and a reference I can name. This rate applies to the first five
engagements only and expires by design.

7 · PAYMENT
50% (₹22,500) to begin · 50% at handover, when your named owners hold the
deliverables and the review calendar is set.

[IF FCRA-FUNDED, add only this line: "Happy to align the contract
structure with your FCRA auditor's guidance." Nothing further.]

Valid 14 days. To proceed, reply confirming and I will send the Terms of
Reference for signature.

Rahul K. Vimal · rkv.consults@gmail.com · +91 9953724719

tor.title: Terms of Reference — OD Engagement
tor.body:
TERMS OF REFERENCE
Between: {{ORG}} ("the Organisation") and Rahul K. Vimal, OD Consultant
("the Consultant") · Date: {{DATE}}

1 · SCOPE
IN: organisational diagnosis (interviews, document review, observation),
scored capacity baseline, diagnostic report, feedback session, action plan.
OUT: implementation of changes, fundraising, legal/financial advice,
anything not written here. Additions are agreed in writing as new scope.

2 · DELIVERABLES & TIMELINE
Capacity baseline + diagnostic report + feedback session + action plan,
within [X] weeks of the start date below.

3 · THE ORGANISATION PROVIDES
A named focal point · access to staff for interviews (confidential; see 6)
· documents on request · leadership at the feedback session · a named owner
per agreed change. If access stops, the timeline pauses; two weeks of
blocked access and either party may close the engagement per clause 8.

4 · FEES & PAYMENT
Total: ₹45,000 (pilot rate, first-five engagements).
50% on signing (work begins on receipt) · 50% at handover — defined as the
deliverables transferred to named owners with a review calendar set. Not
tied to report delivery; tied to handover.

5 · CASE STUDY & REFERENCE (the pilot-rate exchange)
The Organisation agrees to: (a) a written case study naming the
Organisation, describing the engagement and its outcomes, reviewed and
approved by the Organisation before any use; (b) serving as a nameable
reference. Financial figures appear only with separate written consent.

6 · CONFIDENTIALITY
Both ways. The Organisation's internal information stays internal. Staff
interview content is never attributed to a named person without that
person's permission. The Consultant's templates and methods remain the
Consultant's.

7 · MATERIALS
Deliverables belong to the Organisation. The Consultant's underlying
templates, instruments and methods remain the Consultant's and may be
reused elsewhere without the Organisation's data.

8 · CLOSING EARLY
Either party, 7 days' written notice. Fees settle pro-rata against
delivered work.

Signed:
For {{ORG}}: ____________________ Date: ______
Rahul K. Vimal: ____________________ Date: ______

interview-guide.title: Diagnosis Interview Guide (Step 8)
interview-guide.body:
DIAGNOSIS INTERVIEWS — GUIDE
45 minutes each · 6–8 people across board / office / field · notes by hand.

SAY FIRST, EVERY TIME:
"I'm trying to understand how work actually moves here — not to judge
anyone. Nothing you say will be quoted with your name without your
permission. The report describes patterns, not people."

THE QUESTIONS (in order; skip what the role makes irrelevant):
1 · Walk me through yesterday, start to finish.
2 · When [the issue from intake] happens, what do you do, step by step?
3 · How does information reach you — and how do you pass it on?
4 · What happens to your work when you're away for a week?
5 · What did this organisation START doing in the last year, and who made
 that happen? (self-initiated change = adoption capacity)
6 · What tools/registers/formats were started and then stopped? Why?
 (the graveyard — if there are three, format quality is not the problem)
7 · Where does work pile up or stall? Show me if you can.
8 · Who decides [X]? Who do you actually ask when stuck?
9 · Which meeting matters most here? What would break if it stopped?
10 · What does the funder ask for that is hardest to produce?
11 · If you had one free week to fix one thing here, what?
12 · If the founder/director were unreachable for two weeks, what happens?

CLOSE: "What should I have asked that I didn't?"

OBSERVE while on site (don't ask, watch): where records physically live ·
who interrupts whom · what's on the walls · which registers look used vs
decorative · language each document lives in vs language people work in.

AFTER EACH INTERVIEW, note immediately: 3 facts · 1 surprise · 1 pattern
forming · evidence seen (not just claims heard).

capacity-assessment.title: Organisational Capacity Assessment (scored baseline)
capacity-assessment.body:
CAPACITY ASSESSMENT — SCORED BASELINE
Adapted for small Indian NGOs (5–30 staff) from the Marguerite Casey OCAT
lineage. Scored BY THE CONSULTANT from evidence (interviews, documents,
observation) — never self-scored, never from opinion.

SCALE, per item: 1 = absent · 2 = informal/person-dependent ·
3 = written but unevenly used · 4 = systematic and used. Note the EVIDENCE
beside every score. No evidence = score 1, flag it.

A · LEADERSHIP & GOVERNANCE
A1 Board meets and minutes its meetings
A2 Decisions get recorded and communicated, not just made
A3 A second line exists — someone besides the founder can run things
A4 Staff can state what the organisation is trying to achieve this year
A5 Succession/absence: founder away two weeks, work continues

B · MANAGEMENT & OPERATIONS
B1 Roles written; people know who does what
B2 Work is measured by output/result, not attendance/task
B3 The recurring meeting is goal-driven with follow-ups tracked
B4 Task-loads realistic — no chronic single-person overload
B5 Knowledge survives exits — a leaver's work is recoverable

C · SYSTEMS & COMPLIANCE
C1 Core policies exist AND staff can say what's in them
C2 Books monthly, not audit-time; audit filed on time
C3 Statutory current (12A/80G/FCRA-as-applicable/POSH if 10+)
C4 Standard formats: report, budget, proposal — not built fresh each time
C5 A record from last year findable in under ten minutes

D · COMMUNICATION & DELIVERY
D1 Field information reaches the office intact and on time
D2 Funder reporting produced without crisis
D3 Documentation is a habit (a standing agenda item), not an event
D4 Staff have a real channel to raise issues — and use it
D5 External presence (site/social) reflects actual current work

SCORING: 20 items × 1–4 = 20–80.
20–35 FOUNDATIONAL — person-dependent; build the basics first
36–59 EMERGING — pieces exist, no coherent whole; standardise + embed
60–80 SYSTEMATIC — polish, succession and scale questions

Re-run the same instrument at engagement end (Step 12) and at +90 days.
Baseline → endline movement, per item, IS the case study evidence.

call-structure.title: The 20-Minute Scoping Call — structure
call-structure.body:
THE 20-MINUTE CALL — STRUCTURE
Minutes 0-2 · OPEN. Thank them. One sentence on who you are. Then:
"Tell me what's happening." Then be quiet.
Minutes 2-12 · THEIR PROBLEM (the only part that cannot be cut):
· What is not working now? (their words -- write them down verbatim)
· Since when? What has it already cost?
· What have you already tried and stopped?
· What would be different in daily work if this were fixed?
· Who must approve change?
Minutes 12-16 · YOUR HOW (rehearsed, 60 seconds): "I look before I fix.
I spend time understanding how work actually moves -- talking to people,
reading documents, watching -- before proposing anything. Then a small
number of changes your team can genuinely adopt, tested with the people
who will use them, handed over so it runs without me."
Minutes 16-19 · NEXT STEP: "I'll send a short note today on how this
works, and a proposal within 48 hours." NO NUMBER ON THE CALL. If asked:
"I price by scope, not hours -- the proposal ties the number to exactly
what we've discussed."
Minute 20 · Stop on time. Stopping on time IS the first demonstration.
AFTER, within 10 minutes: fill the intake form while memory is fresh.
Within 24 hours: send the Process Note.

holding-reply.title: Holding Reply — when they say yes
holding-reply.body:
Subject: Good to hear from you -- next step

Dear {{CONTACT}},

Thank you for writing back. The right next step is a short call --
twenty minutes, no preparation needed from your side. I mainly want to
understand what's happening in your own words.

Would [DAY, TIME] or [DAY, TIME] work? Happy to adjust.

Rahul
[Send within 24 hours of their reply. Nothing attached. Two time options,
never "whenever suits you" -- open-ended scheduling stalls.]

touch3-value.title: Touch 3 — the pure-value message (day 12)
touch3-value.body:
Subject: Something that may be useful -- no reply needed

Dear {{CONTACT}},

No follow-up ask in this one. I came across [ONE specific thing genuinely
useful to THEM: a funder's new guideline, a relevant scheme deadline, a
report template, a piece on an issue they named]. Sharing because it
relates to what {{ORG}} does: [ONE sentence on why it's relevant to them
specifically].

[LINK or attachment]

Use it freely -- no response needed.

Rahul
[RULES: must be usable whether or not they ever hire you. No pitch, no
"by the way". If you cannot find something genuinely useful, skip Touch 3
rather than send filler.]

engagement-brief.title: Engagement Brief (kickoff, one page)
engagement-brief.body:
ENGAGEMENT BRIEF — {{ORG}} · {{DATE}}
THE ISSUE (their words, from intake): [ ]
AFFECTED: [functions/people]
OBJECTIVE (one sentence, plain): [ ]
IN SCOPE: [ ] OUT OF SCOPE: [ ]
STAKEHOLDERS: decision-maker: [ ] · focal point: [ ] · interviewees: [ ]
TIME FRAME: [start] to [end]
CONSTRAINTS: [budget/season/festivals/field calendar]

SUCCESS INDICATORS — 3 to 5, countable, set NOW before anything changes:
1. [e.g. days field-visit -> report: now 11, target 4]
2. [ ]
3. [ ]
BASELINE VALUES RECORDED ON: [date] BY: [who]
[No indicator without a baseline number. If it cannot be counted, it is
a wish, not an indicator. These exact indicators get re-measured at
Step 12 and at +90 days -- that comparison is the case study.]

doc-checklist.title: Document-Request Checklist (diagnosis)
doc-checklist.body:
DOCUMENTS TO REQUEST — tick what arrives, note what doesn't exist
GOVERNANCE: registration cert · 12A/80G · FCRA (if any) · last 2 board
minutes · org chart (if one exists)
POLICY: every written policy they claim (HR, finance, gender, child
protection, POSH...) -- as USED copies, not master versions
OPERATIONS: 3 recent field reports AS SUBMITTED · monthly progress report
format · last annual report · a proposal that won · one that lost
FINANCE-ADJACENT (never audit them, just flow): budget format · fund
utilisation format · who-approves-what note if written
COMMUNICATION: staff WhatsApp group names/purposes · last 5 outward
letters · website/social links
[WHAT DOESN'T ARRIVE IS DATA. "We have it but can't find it" = finding.
"It's with one person who is travelling" = finding. Note the gaps in the
same list -- they go straight into the diagnostic report.]

confidentiality-note.title: Interviewee Confidentiality Note (hand to each person)
confidentiality-note.body:
BEFORE WE TALK — WHAT HAPPENS TO WHAT YOU SAY
I am {{ORG}}'s organisational development consultant. I am interviewing
people across the organisation to understand how work moves -- not to
evaluate any person.

MY COMMITMENTS TO YOU:
· Nothing you say will be quoted with your name without your permission.
· My report describes PATTERNS, not people.
· I do not report to your manager what you said. Leadership sees themes.
· You may skip any question. You may tell me something is off the record
 -- then it stays out entirely.
· Notes stay with me; they are not shared inside the organisation.

Ask me anything about this before we start.
Rahul K. Vimal · OD Consultant

diagnostic-report.title: Diagnostic Report — template
diagnostic-report.body:
DIAGNOSTIC REPORT — {{ORG}} · {{DATE}}
[WRITING RULES: plain language a field worker reads without slowing down.
Every claim points at evidence. Findings point at the SYSTEM, never at a
person's competence. Thin evidence is labelled hypothesis, not conclusion.]

1 · WHAT I DID: [N] interviews (board/office/field) · [N] documents ·
[N] days observation · capacity assessment (scored separately)
2 · WHAT WORKS -- FIRST. [3-5 real strengths with evidence. Not garnish:
these are what the changes will be BUILT ON.]
3 · FINDINGS. For each (max 5):
 FINDING: [one sentence, plain]
 EVIDENCE: [what was seen/heard/read -- countable where possible]
 COST: [what it causes in daily work]
 ROOT QUESTION: [not "staff don't use the register" but "why is the
 register not usable, known, trusted or reinforced?"]
4 · HYPOTHESES (believed but not proven -- honest section): [ ]
5 · CAPACITY SCORE: [X]/80 -- band + the 3 lowest-scoring items
6 · WHAT I RECOMMEND WE DISCUSS: priorities proposed, DECIDED TOGETHER
 in the feedback session. [3-4 candidate priorities, each: what,
 why now, what it replaces, effort level]
[Report goes to leadership BEFORE the feedback session. Nobody should
hear a finding about their organisation for the first time in a room
full of colleagues.]

feedback-plan.title: Feedback Session — facilitation plan (90 min)
feedback-plan.body:
FEEDBACK SESSION — RUNNING PLAN
WHO: leadership + the people who will own changes. Report sent 2 days prior.
0-10 · FRAME: "Findings describe the system, not persons. Everything is
discussable. We leave with 3 priorities and an owner each."
10-20 · STRENGTHS first -- with evidence. Sets that honesty runs both ways.
20-50 · FINDINGS one at a time: state -> evidence -> their reaction FIRST
("does this match what you see?") -> discuss. Never argue a finding:
"What evidence would change this picture? Let's check it."
50-75 · PRIORITIES: candidate list on the wall. Each rated together:
IMPACT (high/low) x EFFORT (high/low). Do-first = high-impact/low-effort.
High/high = pick ONE. Low-impact anything = parked without guilt.
75-90 · COMMIT: 3 priorities max · one named owner each (a person in the
room, never "the team") · first visible step within 14 days · date of
first review meeting SET NOW, in calendars before the room empties.
IF THE ROOM GOES QUIET: "What would make this list wrong?"
IF ONE VOICE DOMINATES: "I want two more views before we fix this."
OUTPUT same day: one page -- 3 priorities, owners, dates.

action-plan.title: Action Plan + Roadmap — template
action-plan.body:
ACTION PLAN — {{ORG}} · {{DATE}}
[Made only AFTER the Clarity gate. Per change, every column filled --
an empty column means the change is not ready to plan.]

FOR EACH CHANGE (3 max):
· THE CHANGE, one sentence: [ ]
· REPLACES: [what stops when this starts -- nothing may only ADD work]
· OWNER: [named person] · DOER(S): [who does it day to day]
· LIVES IN: [which EXISTING meeting/routine carries it -- no slot = no
 heartbeat = it will die]
· FORCING FUNCTION: [what external thing checks it: funder format, audit,
 review meeting agenda]
· FIRST VISIBLE STEP by [date, within 14 days]: [ ]
· INDICATOR (from Engagement Brief): [which number this moves]
· PILOT: [smallest real test -- one village/team/month -- before scaling]
ROADMAP: Weeks 1-2 pilot starts · W3-4 pilot review vs indicator, adjust
· W5-8 scale or stop ("do not scale what is not adopted") · W8+ owner
runs it, consultant steps back.
IMPACT x EFFORT decided in the feedback session. This document only ever
contains do-first and chosen high/high items.

handover-pack.title: Handover Pack (+ ownership matrix & review calendar)
handover-pack.body:
HANDOVER PACK — {{ORG}} · {{DATE}}
1 · WHAT WAS BUILT: [each deliverable: name · version · where it lives ·
in what language]
2 · OWNERSHIP MATRIX:
[System/practice] -> [Owner (named)] -> [Backup person] -> [Where it
lives] -> [Review rhythm]
(A system with no backup person is a future single-point failure --
flag it here honestly rather than leave it silent.)
3 · REVIEW CALENDAR: which existing meeting reviews each practice, how
often, first three dates WRITTEN IN.
4 · VERSION RULE: every tool carries version number + owner + last-review
date. Editing without bumping the version = two truths in circulation.
5 · WHAT REMAINS OPEN: [unfinished items, honestly listed, with whose
court they sit in]
6 · CONSULTANT EXIT: what I will still answer (quick questions, 90-day
check) and what now belongs to you (everything else).
SIGN: Organisation focal point ______ · Consultant ______ · Date ______
[Tranche 2 releases at THIS document's signing -- with named owners,
not at report delivery.]

case-study-request.title: Case Study + Reference Request (at handover)
case-study-request.body:
[ASK AT THE HANDOVER MEETING ITSELF -- goodwill is highest the day they
receive everything. Never months later.]

Say: "As we agreed at the start -- the pilot rate was exchanged for a
written case study and a reference. I'll do the writing; you approve
every word before it's used anywhere."

THEN SEND, same day:
Dear {{CONTACT}},
Thank you for today. As discussed, here is the draft case study
[ATTACH: 1 page -- situation, what was done, what changed WITH the
baseline->endline numbers, one quote from you if you're comfortable].
Please mark anything to change or remove -- nothing is used without your
written approval. Two smaller requests: (1) may I name {{ORG}} publicly
as a client, and (2) would you be open to a short reference call if a
future organisation asks?
Financial figures stay out unless you separately approve them in writing.
Rahul
[If they hesitate on naming: anonymous version ("a Rajasthan NGO working
on land rights") still has value. Take what is freely given.]

lesson-log.title: Lesson Log (fill within one week of handover)
lesson-log.body:
LESSON LOG — {{ORG}} · closed {{DATE}}
CONTEXT: [org, size, funder, issue type from intake]
INTERVENTION: [what was actually built/changed]
EVIDENCE USED: [what the diagnosis actually rested on]
ADOPTION: [what they took up · what they resisted · why, honestly]
RESULTS: [baseline -> endline numbers; "not yet measurable" is a valid
entry -- an invented number is not]
ASSUMPTIONS THAT PROVED WRONG: [the section that matters most. What did
you believe at intake that turned out false? What did you scope that
they didn't need? What did they need that you missed?]
DO DIFFERENTLY NEXT TIME: [1-3 concrete changes to the process itself]
REUSABLE: [templates/formats built here worth filing for the next
engagement -- file them NOW, not "later"]
+90-DAY CHECK booked for: [date, in calendar] -- one question: "is it
still being used?"
[By engagement four, this file is worth more than the case studies.]

process-note.title: OD Process & Approach Note (client-facing)
process-note.body:
ORGANISATIONAL DEVELOPMENT ENGAGEMENT — PROCESS & APPROACH NOTE
Prepared by: Rahul K. Vimal — OD Consultant, C4D Practitioner
For: {{ORG}} · Date: {{DATE}}

1 · PURPOSE OF THIS DOCUMENT
This note explains how the OD process will work, step by step -- so your
team knows what to expect, what you will receive, and what is needed from
you. It is not a contract; it is a shared map before we begin.

2 · WHAT OD IS -- AND WHY IT MATTERS FOR YOU
Organisational Development strengthens the human system of an organisation
-- its governance, people, systems and culture -- so it can deliver its
mission reliably. Organisations don't change unless the people inside them
do. OD is not a one-off training or a set of documents; it is a structured
process that diagnoses the real issue, builds the right systems, and
leaves your team able to sustain the change.

3 · THE PROCESS, PHASE BY PHASE
1. ENTRY & CONTRACTING -- we agree scope, goals, access, confidentiality
   and what success looks like, in writing. You receive: Terms of Reference.
2. DIAGNOSIS -- interviews (board, staff, field), review of your documents,
   and an organisational capacity assessment. You receive: a scored baseline.
3. FEEDBACK -- findings presented to leadership in a working session;
   priorities agreed together. You receive: the diagnostic report.
4. ACTION PLANNING -- priorities become a concrete roadmap with measurable
   indicators. You receive: the action plan.
5. IMPLEMENTATION -- we build the agreed systems: policies, formats,
   training, coaching. You receive: the working tools, tested with your team.
6. EVALUATION -- capacity re-measured against the baseline: did the system
   shift? You receive: the evaluation note.
7. EXIT & HANDOVER -- internal owners named, systems documented, review
   rhythm set. You receive: the handover pack.

4 · WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU
A single focal point for scheduling · honest access to people and documents
· leadership presence at the feedback and planning sessions · owners
assigned for each system, so it survives handover.

5 · HOW WE WORK
Evidence before recommendations. Adoption before documentation -- a policy
nobody uses is a liability. Simplicity before complexity. Your context
before any framework. Bilingual delivery (Hindi and English).
Confidential -- your internal information stays internal. Capacity-first:
the goal is that you don't need us afterward.

6 · ABOUT THE CONSULTANT
Rahul K. Vimal -- MSc Applied Social Psychology (HSE University, Moscow);
OD consultant and C4D practitioner. OD engagements delivered in India,
alongside four years of partnership work across MENA, Europe, Latin
America and APAC, and study and fellowship experience in Russia and Israel.

7 · NEXT STEPS
1. You review this note and raise questions.
2. We hold a 30-minute scoping call.
3. We finalise the Terms of Reference and begin Phase 1.
Contact: rkv.consults@gmail.com · +91 9953724719

touch1-email.title: First-Touch Email — rules + skeleton
touch1-email.body:
FIRST-TOUCH EMAIL — THE RULES
· Under 90 words, total.
· ONE specific, verifiable thing about THEM -- from their own site or a
  publication, checked the same morning. Never broker-scraped data.
· No compliment sandwich. No "I hope this finds you well."
· Ask for a conversation, not a sale. Twenty minutes.
· "Dear [Name]," -- a real name, or the email does not go.
· Attach NOTHING. No profile, no rate, no brochure.
· End where the thought ends.

SKELETON:
Subject: [something specific to them, not to you]

Dear [Name],

[One sentence: the specific, verifiable thing you noticed about their
work -- an account of a real transition, a programme detail, their own
published words.] [One sentence: why that specific thing is a real test
or moment for an organisation.]

I am an OD consultant. I work on [one line matched to what you noticed].

Twenty minutes?

Rahul

[TEST BEFORE SENDING: if the first sentence could be pasted into an email
to any other organisation, it is not specific enough. Rewrite or don't send.]

entry-criteria.title: Entry Criteria — the five tests before any outreach
entry-criteria.body:
THE FIVE TESTS — an organisation qualifies only if ALL five hold:
1 · A REAL OPERATIONAL PAIN POINT -- something specific is breaking, not
    just "they got funding" or "they seem like they need help."
2 · LEADERSHIP WILLING TO ENGAGE HONESTLY -- signs they can hear findings
    about their own organisation.
3 · STAFF ACCESS IS POSSIBLE -- diagnosis needs interviews; a leader who
    will answer for everyone is a red flag at the door.
4 · EVIDENCE CAN BE REVIEWED -- documents, processes, real work products.
5 · OPEN TO PHASED IMPROVEMENT -- small pilots first, not a demand for
    transformation by Friday.

REMEMBER: a funding announcement is a SIGNAL, not a qualification. Run
these five before a single word of outreach is drafted. Fail any one =
no outreach; record why, move on. The gate working looks like fewer
drafts, not more.

readiness-check.title: NGO Readiness Self-Check (front-door, 10 minutes)
readiness-check.body:
NGO READINESS SELF-CHECK
For the organisation to fill in ~10 minutes. Score each 0-4
(0 = not at all · 4 = fully, and used). This is a conversation starter,
not a verdict.

1 · GOVERNANCE & FOOTING: registered and current? 12A/80G in place? FCRA
    status clear? A board that actually meets and records its meetings?
2 · POLICIES ON PAPER: HR, finance, gender/safeguarding -- documents that
    exist and are used, or things "everyone knows"?
3 · FORMATS READY: a report format a donor would accept? A proposal
    template? A budget format? Or is every document built from zero,
    under deadline?
4 · THE KEY-PERSON TEST: if the founder is unavailable for two weeks,
    does work continue? Does one person hold all passwords, relationships
    and knowledge?
5 · FINANCIAL HYGIENE: books monthly (not at audit time)? Last audit
    filed on time? A fund-utilisation statement producible on request?
6 · COMMUNICATION: can the team write to a funder without outside help?
    Do reports tell what changed, or only list activities?

SCORE: 0-8 foundations first · 9-16 pieces exist, no whole ·
17-24 donor-ready, polish remains.
[Offer this freely -- it is useful to them whether or not they ever hire
you. That is exactly why it works as the pure-value touch.]
